record.paper_title: Dima Khavinson’s 60th: a summary of open problems in analysis and mathematical physics
record.original_question: Let w = e^u be a logarithmically subharmonic weight on the unit disk D, let A_w^2 be the corresponding weighted Bergman space, and let K_w(z, ξ) be its reproducing kernel. For every N, must every linear combination Σ_{j=0}^N λ_j (∂/∂ξ)^j K_w(z, ξ)|_{ξ=0} have only O(N) zeros in D? And does an analogous O(N) bound also hold for finite sums Σ_{j=0}^N λ_j K_w(z, ξ_j) with ξ_j in D?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 5.1 Any linear combination Σ λj (∂/∂ξ)^j Kw(z,ξ)|ξ=0 has at most O(N) zeros in D.
Also, a similar estimate should hold if, instead of linear combination (5.1), one considers Σ λj Kw(z, ξj), ξj ∈ D.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ denote the open unit disk. Let $u:\mathbb{D}\to[-\infty,\infty)$ be a subharmonic function and set $w=e^u$, so that $w$ is a logarithmically subharmonic weight on $\mathbb{D}$. Consider the weighted Bergman space
$$A_w^2(\mathbb{D}) = \Big\{ f \text{ holomorphic on } \mathbb{D} : \|f\|_w^2 := \int_{\mathbb{D}} |f(z)|^2 \, w(z)\, dA(z) < \infty \Big\},$$
where $dA$ is area measure. Assume $A_w^2(\mathbb{D})$ is a (non-trivial) reproducing kernel Hilbert space, with reproducing kernel $K_w(z,\xi)$ characterized by $f(\xi) = \langle f, K_w(\cdot,\xi)\rangle_w$ for every $f\in A_w^2(\mathbb{D})$ and every $\xi\in\mathbb{D}$.

(a) Prove or disprove: there exists an absolute constant $C>0$ (possibly depending on $w$) such that for every nonnegative integer $N$ and every choice of complex coefficients $\lambda_0,\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_N$, not all zero, the function
$$z \mapsto \sum_{j=0}^{N} \lambda_j \left.\frac{\partial^j}{\partial \bar\xi^j} K_w(z,\xi)\right|_{\xi=0}$$
has at most $C\cdot N$ zeros in $\mathbb{D}$ (counted with multiplicity), i.e. an $O(N)$ bound.

(b) Prove or disprove the analogous statement: for every $N$, every choice of points $\xi_0,\dots,\xi_N\in\mathbb{D}$, and every choice of complex coefficients $\lambda_0,\dots,\lambda_N$ (not all zero), the function
$$z \mapsto \sum_{j=0}^{N} \lambda_j K_w(z,\xi_j)$$
has at most $O(N)$ zeros in $\mathbb{D}$.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search for the conjecture on $O(N)$ bounds for zeros of linear combinations of weighted Bergman reproducing kernels with logarithmically subharmonic weights returned related work on weighted Bergman kernels (Shimorin-type representations, subharmonicity of the diagonal, Suita-type problems) but no source confirming a resolution of this specific conjecture. The current status appears unverified.

status_evidence.title: On the converse of the Shimorin–Peláez–Rättyä–Wick theorem
status_evidence.snippet: Necessary and sufficient conditions for a Shimorin kernel to be the kernel of a radial, logarithmically subharmonic weighted Bergman space; non-radial case remains open.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work on the same family of weighted Bergman kernels does not settle the zero-counting conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Weighted Bergman Kernels and Mathematical Physics
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing weighted Bergman kernels for log-subharmonic weights and connected open problems.
status_evidence.claim: No proof or disproof of the O(N) zero bound is reported in recent surveys.
